concepts.def: The right amounts of carbohydrate, protein, lipid, vitamins, minerals, fibre and water.

walkthroughs.body_html:
Human Nutrition — a core area of GCSE Biology.

Working through it builds the schema you need: the key terms, how they connect, and how to use them together.

Human Nutrition brings together several ideas you need to use as a set, not in isolation.

Lock in the vocabulary first, then practise pulling the ideas together to answer real questions.

Use the activities in this adventure to build familiarity with Human Nutrition.

Practise vocabulary, calculations and free-text questions to lock in the learning.

mcqs.q: The enzyme that digests starch is:
options: amylase
protease
lipase
catalase

mcqs.q: Villi increase the rate of absorption mainly because they:
options: increase the surface area of the small intestine
produce more digestive enzymes
speed up peristalsis
make bile in the gut wall

mcqs.q: The role of bile in digestion is to:
options: emulsify fats into small droplets
digest proteins into amino acids
break starch into sugars
absorb amino acids into the blood

mcqs.q: A diet lacking vitamin C can cause:
options: scurvy
rickets
anaemia
goitre

mcqs.q: Where is most digested food absorbed?
options: Most absorption happens in the small intestine, whose villi give a huge surface area for absorbing soluble food molecules.
Food is absorbed mainly in the large intestine.
Food is absorbed mainly in the stomach.
Bile breaks proteins down into amino acids.
Bile is an enzyme that digests fats.
Bile breaks proteins down into amino acids.
Bile emulsifies fats into small droplets, increasing their surface area for lipase, and it neutralises acidic stomach contents.
Chewing has no role in digestion at all.

mcqs.q: Does chewing food count as chemical digestion?
options: Chewing has no role in digestion at all.
Chewing is chemical digestion because it breaks food down.
Bile breaks proteins down into amino acids.
No - chewing is physical (mechanical) digestion; chemical digestion is the breakdown of molecules by enzymes.

mcqs.q: Which of these is the best definition of “Peristalsis”?
options: Waves of muscle contraction in the wall of the gut that push food along the alimentary canal.
Tiny finger-like projections lining the small intestine that provide a large surface area for the efficient absorption of digested food.
The breakdown of large, insoluble food molecules into small, soluble molecules that can be absorbed into the blood.
A diet containing carbohydrates, proteins, fats, vitamins, minerals, fibre and water in the correct proportions to keep the body healthy.

mcqs.q: Which of these is the best definition of “Balanced diet”?
options: A green liquid made in the liver and stored in the gall bladder that emulsifies fats into droplets and neutralises stomach acid.
A diet containing carbohydrates, proteins, fats, vitamins, minerals, fibre and water in the correct proportions to keep the body healthy.
A digestive enzyme made in the salivary glands and pancreas that breaks down starch into the sugar maltose.
Waves of muscle contraction in the wall of the gut that push food along the alimentary canal.

sequence.def: Teeth chew; amylase begins starch digestion
Peristalsis pushes the bolus to the stomach
Enzymes finish digestion; nutrients absorbed by villi
Water absorbed from the remaining material
Faeces stored and egested through the anus
